design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (difficulty weekly_certification_and_benefit_payment, category claim). Revision 2 (policy-task audit round 1 closed; see [Revision log]).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5,6,4,5]; disallowance 5, waiting-week value 5, holiday-pay report 4, weekly payment 6.
[Scope] Task 0 holds the dependency redetermination, payment election, supplemental correction and Extended Benefits determination. This task claims claim_ext_dependency_disallowance (record_dependency_disallowance_f94a20ca), claim_ext_waiting_week_value (record_waiting_week_428070c9), claim_ext_holiday_pay_report (certify_week_by_phone_ea18d1f2, owner user) and claim_ext_regular_weekly_payable (issue_weekly_payment_6cd10c49). Together the two scopes cover all eight policies, pairwise disjoint.
[Why a good test] The caller asks only to be paid for the week ending 2026-09-12. The weekly-payment rule waits on a waiting-week entry for the first otherwise-payable week (none stands), an allowance that no longer counts the removed dependent (30.00 still counts two), and the claimant's own certification of the week paid (missing). The waiting-week value waits on the allowance, and certifying a later week waits on the waiting-week entry, so the only order is disallowance, waiting week, certification, payment. Each write carries a 4-6 factor computation over the claim, the earlier claim's 23 certifications, and three other products (appeal, withholding, overpayment).
[Problem tree card] Root claim_ext_regular_weekly_payable. (1) payment <- waiting week, value_input, gate served, state: 'A weekly payment is not fixed until the claim carries a waiting-week entry for the first otherwise-payable week of its benefit year.' — false: the claim ledger holds only the 2026-09-03 credit. (2) payment <- disallowance, value_input, gate da, state: 'A weekly payment is fixed only after the claim's dependency allowance no longer counts any dependent removed from the record.' — false: allowance 30.00 with dependents_count 1. (3) payment <- certification (USER), value_input, gate opay, state: 'A weekly payment is issued only after the week being paid carries the claimant's weekly certification.' — false: no certification of 2026-09-12. (4) waiting week <- disallowance, value_input, state: 'The value of a waiting week is not fixed until the claim's dependency allowance no longer counts any dependent removed from the record.'. (5) certification <- waiting week, state_gate, state: 'A week after the first week of a benefit year is certified only after the claim carries a waiting-week entry.'. One write of the difficulty records waiting-week entries, one records certifications, and only the disallowance lowers an allowance for a removed dependent (task 0's redetermination adds dependents). The weekly rule now states the waiting-week dependency once (the prerequisite sentence only). Deletion sensitivity: claim_ext_regular_weekly_payable -> claim_ext_waiting_week_value: Without the waiting-week entry the weekly payment computes 0 instead of 477.; claim_ext_regular_weekly_payable -> claim_ext_dependency_disallowance: Without the disallowance the weekly payment is 485 instead of 477 (allowance 30.00).; claim_ext_regular_weekly_payable -> claim_ext_holiday_pay_report: Without the certification the latest certified week is 2026-09-05 and the payment computes 429 for the wrong week.; claim_ext_waiting_week_value -> claim_ext_dependency_disallowance: Without the disallowance the waiting-week value is 435 instead of 430.; claim_ext_holiday_pay_report -> claim_ext_waiting_week_value: With the certification first, the waiting-week value reads the week ending 2026-09-12 and becomes 425 instead of 430; the terminal waiting-week entry differs..
[Base-invariant card] Waiting week: waiting_week_once — no entry on the claim (0 below 1); a week reaching the program's 32-hour threshold would not serve (17.0 h does). Certification: opens Sunday 2026-09-13 (offset 1, inclusive), claim active, none for 2026-09-12, 3 days after the week -> timely. Weekly payment: claim active, no payment for 2026-09-12 on any claim, kind weekly, waiting week served after the earlier write. Disallowance (claim_entitlement_reduced): claim_monetary_eligibility, policy_scope.
[Business-object card] Claim 45e35e66-8b7d-4d54-a6a0-f95ae7f7e8a8 (UCFE, effective 2026-08-30). Waiting week 2026-09-05 (17.0 h, 272.00). Paid week 2026-09-12 (7.0 h, 112.00, Labor Day holiday pay). Earlier claim 71af817e-3d50-46fa-b239-bc20a5566f5a (closed 2026-08-29) supplies the hardware-store hours and earnings. Cross products: monetary appeal (scheduled 2026-09-29), current-support withholding order (requested, effective 2026-09-28: no deduction due today), overpayment (Non-Fraud — Claimant Error, misreported earnings, determined 2026-05-12, repaid in full 2026-05-29 before recovery began: status paid_in_full, consistent with the overpay charter's established -> paid_in_full transition).
[Factor card] RED: remaining_dependent_amount (parameter): evidence claim_age = 16, per_dep = 18.00; tier taken: 'exactly one dependent remains on record and the claim is fewer than the long-claim days old'; its baseline (P('dependency_allowance_per_dependent')) gives result 140 instead of 135. | disallowance_weeks (method): evidence paid_weeks = 0, weeks = 25; tier taken: 'no weekly payment issued on the claim'; its baseline (P('max_duration_weeks')) gives result 140 instead of 135. | provisional_allowance_ceiling (parameter): evidence det_age = 12, da_new = 19.20; tier taken: 'the latest monetary determination no more than the redetermination window days old'; its baseline (RND(per_dep * counted, 2)) gives result 93 instead of 135. | pending_monetary_appeal_share (parameter, cross-difficulty appeal): evidence ap_status = scheduled, ap_outcome = pending, ap_share = 0.50; tier taken: 'the claimant's Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination on the claim stands filed or scheduled'; its baseline (1) gives result 270 instead of 135. | supported_removed_dependent (parameter, cross-difficulty withhold): evidence cs_active = 0, cs_requested = 1, extra_dep = 0.25; tier taken: 'none stands active or suspended and at least one such order stands at status requested'; its baseline (0) gives result 150 instead of 135. | all baselines -> 390. WW: waiting_disregard_share (parameter): evidence wk_earn = 272.00, share = 0.40; tier taken: 'dependents on record and the week reports earnings'; its baseline (P('earnings_disregard_pct_of_wba')) gives result 406 instead of 430. | waiting_hours_base (parameter): evidence recall_days = 216, thr = 36; tier taken: 'a definite recall date no more than the near-recall days after the handling date'; its baseline (P('full_time_hours_threshold')) gives result 399 instead of 430. | waiting_excess_rate (parameter): evidence hours = 17.00, earn_ded = 60.00; tier taken: 'hours below the low fraction of the hours base'; its baseline (excess) gives result 370 instead of 430. | waiting_allowance_counted (method): evidence gross_q = 272.00, da_counted = 10.13; tier taken: 'earnings above the disregard and hours at least the quarter fraction of the hours base'; its baseline (da) gives result 439 instead of 430. | waiting_integrity_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty overpay): evidence op_open = 0.00, op_count = 1, integrity = 40.00; tier taken: 'such overpayments determined within the window exist and all carry no balance due'; its baseline (0) gives result 450 instead of 430. | all baselines -> 371. CT: holiday_history_window (parameter): evidence closed_age = 17, win = 12; tier taken: 'the earlier claim closed no more than the recent-closure days before the handling date'; its baseline (K('win_standard')) gives result 69.00 instead of 73.26. | holiday_regular_rate (method): evidence g_w = 4167.50, h_w = 256.00, lat_g = 227.50, rate = 16.28; tier taken: 'window hours at least the minimum hours'; its baseline (RND(F('high_quarter_wages') / K('quarter_hours'), 2)) gives result 103.50 instead of 73.26. | holiday_hours_credited (parameter): evidence lat_h = 14.00, hol_hours = 6; tier taken: 'at least the short-week hours but fewer than the mid-week hours'; its baseline (K('hol_std')) gives result 97.68 instead of 73.26. | holiday_pay_share (parameter): evidence n_w = 23, avg_h = 11.13, share = 0.75; tier taken: 'at least the low-average hours but below the mid-average hours'; its baseline (1) gives result 97.68 instead of 73.26. | all baselines -> 184.0. WP: weekly_disregard_share (parameter): evidence recall_days = 216, share = 0.40; tier taken: 'a definite recall date no more than the near-recall days after the handling date and the week reports earnings'; its baseline (P('earnings_disregard_pct_of_wba')) gives result 453 instead of 477. | weekly_full_time_threshold (parameter): evidence claim_age = 16, thr = 36; tier taken: 'a federal separation on the claim and the claim fewer than the new-claim days old'; its baseline (P('full_time_hours_threshold')) gives result 472 instead of 477. | weekly_excess_rate (parameter): evidence hours = 7.00, earn_ded = 16.63; tier taken: 'hours below the low fraction of the threshold'; its baseline (excess) gives result 461 instead of 477. | weekly_allowance_paid (parameter): evidence hours_q = 7.0, da_paid = 14.40; tier taken: 'counted earnings above the disregard and hours below the part-week fraction'; its baseline (da) gives result 482 instead of 477. | weekly_holiday_treatment (method): evidence hol_hours_check = 7.00, counted_gross = 185.26, hol_ded = 0; tier taken: 'holiday pay reported and the claimant worked fewer than one day's hours (but some hours) in the week'; its baseline (gross; (opay if opay_type == 'holiday_pay' or opay_type == 'vacation_pay' else (RND(opay * P('pension_offset_pct'), 2) if opay_type == 'pension_employer_funded' else (RND(opay * P('pension_offset_pct_claimant_contributed'), 2) if opay_type == 'pension_claimant_contributed' else 0)))) gives result 425 instead of 477. | weekly_integrity_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty overpay): evidence op_open = 0.00, op_count = 1, integrity = 40.00; tier taken: 'such overpayments determined within the window exist and all carry no balance due'; its baseline (0) gives result 499 instead of 477. | all baselines -> 425. Genuine method factors: disallowance_weeks (balance-based weeks vs duration less waiting weeks vs duration), waiting_allowance_counted (allowance prorated by unworked hours vs a three-quarter multiplier vs full), holiday_regular_rate (window average vs latest week vs wage-record rate; its fall-through is now exactly the baseline rate), weekly_holiday_treatment (holiday pay moved into earnings vs half deducted vs standard deduction). Excess-rate and history-window factors are labelled parameter. Multi-source: waiting_disregard_share (dependents on the claim AND the week's earnings on the certification) and weekly_disregard_share (recall date on the claim AND the week's earnings); remaining_dependent_amount tests two fields of the claim row and is not counted as multi-source. Cross-difficulty: pending_monetary_appeal_share (appeal), waiting/weekly integrity reduction (overpay), supported_removed_dependent (withhold). Near-misses: the closed claim's 24 weekly payments and waiting week; the current claim's 2026-09-05 certification inside the holiday window but on another claim; 17.0 h vs the 18-hour line; 7.0 h vs the 7.2-hour part-week line.
[Overrides] Declared: weekly payment — earnings, full-time, other-pay and payable-amount sentences of claim_evt_payable_amount; disallowance — booking, dependency-allowance and maximum-benefit sentences of claim_monetary_eligibility. The waiting-week value now follows base serving rules (program threshold; no entry once the count is served) and states its other-pay deduction in full; the holiday-pay report adds a value base never computes.
[World rows] customers 1; claims 2; claim_certifications 26; claim_ledger 27; idv_cases 2; overpayments 1; overpay_ledger 2 (assessment, repayment); appeals 1; appeal_events 1; withholding_orders 1. No active order, no overpayment balance, UCFE non-charged: no deduction, offset or charge is owed.
[Persona] Thaddeus volunteers only his goal; identity on request; family, appeal and the repaid overpayment only when asked; he certifies himself with his stated answers and the holiday pay and timeliness the agent tells him; closes when told the payment is issued.
[Standard solution] Locate, verify; read claims, certifications, ledger, identity cases, overpayments and their ledger, claim requests, appeals and the hearing setting, withholding orders; disallowance (19.20, 135); waiting week 2026-09-05 (430); claimant certifies 2026-09-12 with holiday pay 73.26; weekly payment 477 by direct deposit to checking.
[Verification run] check_compute's build_env/eval_compute on handling-time worlds replayed with the real tools: RED 135, WW 430, CT 73.26, WP 477.
[No real-world waits] All writes land at 2026-09-15 15:10 CDT; the hearing date and the order's effective date are recorded facts, not waits.
[Revision log] Round 2 (audit revision_1): F-3 allowance and maximum-benefit sentences declared superseded by the disallowance; F-2b payable-amount sentence declared superseded by the weekly payment; F-4 waiting-week serving follows base (own hours base used only for partial-week fractions); F-6 waiting-week other pay stated in full; F-8 excess rates and history window relabelled parameter, waiting-week allowance made a prorating method; F-9 holiday rate baseline reduced to the wage-record rate so the ladder's fall-through is the baseline; F-10 integrity tiers rebuilt on balance due and made disjoint; overpay seed made charter-consistent (claimant error cannot be waiver-pending: now repaid in full; waiting value 429 -> 430); persona's recall-waiver line narrowed; false multi-source claim removed; O-8 duplicate waiting wording removed; O-10 pensions restored in the weekly other-pay deduction; earlier rounding tie fix (week 2026-02-21 earnings 227.50) kept.
[Revision log] Round 5 (KB audit, policy-side notes): rule and compute aligned without moving any value — weekly full-time threshold sentence states both its uses and the allowance-paid tier reads the week's hours; the disallowance counts current-support orders binding the claimant by status (XCOUNT) instead of reading one order; the election's verification tiers read the most recently verified case of each kind (XLATEST); the holiday baseline no longer lists the unused minimum-hours constant; the weekly benefit amount is attributed to the allowance-ceiling factors of the redetermination and disallowance; the EB baseline states the training addition as a zero step; the stale 'penalty share' note is gone.
user_scenario: You are Thaddeus Okonkwo-Lindqvist, 41, a seasonal interpretive ranger whose federal summer tour at the national lakeshore ended at the end of August; on weekends you also work a few hours at a hardware store in town. You filed your federal unemployment claim online on September 1. You are calling on a Tuesday afternoon, friendly and a bit rushed, using short sentences. You open by saying you have not received any unemployment payment yet and you would like to get paid for last week, the week ending 2026-09-12 (the Labor Day week). That is all you ask for. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name and your phone number 6085551562; when asked for more, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 1739, and your date of birth, 1985-07-09. If asked, your email is thaddeus.okonkwolindqvist@lakelandmail.net and your ZIP code is 53716. You do not know your weekly amount, balance or any figures and ask the agent to look them up. If the agent asks about your first week, you say you certified it online on September 6 and worked 17 hours at the hardware store that week. Only if the agent asks about your family do you say that your younger daughter now lives with her mother, who claims her on her own unemployment claim, and that a child support order for her came in the mail last week but has not started yet. Only if the agent asks about appeals do you say you appealed your monetary determination because wages from your second federal job were missing and that your hearing is set for September 29. Only if the agent asks about any overpayment do you say you had an overpayment in May because you misreported some earnings on your old claim, and that you paid it back in full at the end of May. When the agent explains that you need to certify the week ending 2026-09-12 yourself, you agree, and once the agent hands you the phone-line certification step you carry it out yourself with these answers: you were able and available all week, you refused no work, you worked 7.0 hours on Saturday and earned 112.00 gross, you made 0 work-search contacts because the office told you your search is waived for your first eight weeks since you have a recall date, and your employer paid you holiday pay for Labor Day, but your pay stub is not out yet so you do not know the dollar amount and you enter exactly the holiday pay amount and the timeliness choice the agent tells you to enter. If the agent asks whether it may record what it needs on your claim, you say yes, go ahead. Your payments should keep going to the checking account on file, and you say so if asked. You never suggest steps, rules or numbers yourself and you do not correct the agent. Once the agent tells you the payment for that week has been issued, you thank them and end the call.
